A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NAG research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results, guidance-coefficient experiments, qualitative examples, and an eight-evaluator user study in Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 reports original benchmark results, a ten-evaluator user study, and sensitivity and generation-order experiments.

M1.justification: v3 adopts descending ImageBind text-video similarity order for sequential generation (Section 5.1 and Appendix F). Its random-order results reproduce v1's earlier NAG scores, supporting a limited generation-order refinement. The NAG guidance equation, ControlNet mechanism, frozen MMAudio backbone, and training loss remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions train with VGGSound, Clotho, AudioCaps, and WavCaps and evaluate on Multi-Caps VGGSound. Caption-order variants and additional evaluators change procedures and sample size, without adding datasets, domains, or task coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Seeing-and-Hearing, FoleyCrafter, and MMAudio-S-16k, including the same independent-generation, negative-prompting, and fused-caption reference configurations. The user-study comparator remains independent MMAudio-S-16k; the new order experiment tests NAG variants.

E3.justification: v3 compares random, ascending, and descending caption orders and uses descending order for its main results. Appendix A increases evaluators from 8 to 10, individual-track responses from 320 to 400, and composite responses from 40 to 50. The five-video study sample and evaluation questions remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix F and Table A3 test whether generating prominent or subtle events first affects composite quality. The guidance-coefficient sensitivity experiment and existing spectrogram case studies are retained, including the appendix examples renumbered from Figure A5 to Figure A4.

E5.justification: Both versions report individual user ratings as mean plus or minus standard deviation and benchmark scores as point estimates. No run-count, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing procedure is added or revised. The increased evaluator count is a sample-size change.

E6.justification: Tables 1, 2, and A1 and the preference plot contain updated results. Main NAG FDPANNs changes from 7.32 to 6.47 under descending ordering; v3 retains 7.32 for random order in Table A3, so this is not a same-setting gain. With the larger user-study sample, audio-quality preference wins change from 52.5% to 58%. Table A3 also adds order-dependent results.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 removes v1's joint two-track factorization and approximation in Equations (4)-(5), including the sufficient-statistic argument for dropping C1. v3 directly defines the next-track conditional-generation objective. The concept-negation mathematics and Appendix B derivation remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions claim incremental generation of complementary, separable audio tracks, improved composite audio, and training without specialized multi-reference datasets. v3's stronger emphasis on incremental completion and subjective evaluation clarifies retained contributions rather than introducing a different core claim.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the new order experiment as evidence that generating prominent events first improves quality. Existing explanations concerning sound contamination, rare-sound failures, and dependence on the base model remain. The mixing limitation moves from the conclusion to Appendix G rather than being newly introduced.

D1.justification: Expanded Appendix D discloses six ControlNet blocks for twelve backbone blocks, attention dimensions matching MMAudio-S-16k, 107M ControlNet parameters, and 2.07 seconds per generation step on an H100. These are additional details, not evidence of architectural changes. v3 also identifies a supplementary demo path; existing training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The reference lists contain the same works after formatting differences are removed. Positioning relative to positive audio conditioning, generative add operations, and concept-negation approaches remains substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: Rewriting concentrates on the abstract, introduction, and shortened problem setup. v3 replaces 'audio independency' with 'audio separability,' integrates subjective evaluation into the main results, and consolidates limitations in the appendix. The overall section sequence and most technical exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 gains feedback arrows showing previously generated audio. v3 adds Table A3, moves the updated preference plot from Appendix A to main Figure 5, and places Tables 1 and 2 together. Title/header typography and page layout change, while the other method diagrams and qualitative examples are retained.

improvement.justification: The generation-order experiment supplies useful evidence for a practical design choice, expanded Appendix D improves reproducibility, and the existing user study gains two evaluators. These provide a modest quality improvement. Minor editorial inconsistencies remain, including obsolete equation references and the retained 'except IS' statement despite Table 1's revised scores, but they do not outweigh the added evidence and documentation.
